issues.description: LANGUAGE-SELECTION PATTERN MIRRORS THE OCR BUG (concern A reference). The recognizer's language is fixed at session start from a single user/default choice: `startRecording(language: selectedLanguage)` where `selectedLanguage` defaults to `.english` (line 36) and is only re-seeded from translationDirection in `.onAppear` (line 195). Recognition does NOT auto-switch by what is actually spoken — if the user leaves it on English and speaks Mandarin, the en-US SpeechTranscriber produces wrong/garbage output until the user manually changes the picker and restarts. This is the speech-domain analogue of the reported OCR symptom 'stuck detecting English, cannot read Mandarin'. The fix model for OCR is the same: either let the user pick the Vision/recognition language explicitly OR run language detection first and feed the correct locale into recognitionLanguages.

LANGUAGE DETECTION IS A NAIVE CHINESE-CHARACTER SCAN, NOT NLLanguageRecognizer. Source language for translation is decided purely by `transcript.contains { $0.isChineseCharacter }` (transcriptContainsChinese, lines 63-65; reused at line 720). There is no NLLanguageRecognizer usage anywhere in this subsystem. For OCR/AI work (A) this is the key seam: the codebase currently has no robust language-detection primitive, so any 'detect language then choose recognitionLanguages' logic must be built. The same heuristic (`isChineseCharacter`) is the only language signal available and would also misroute mixed/short/punctuation-only strings.

RECOGNITION CONFIG IS MINIMAL AND HARD-CODED. The SpeechTranscriber is built with empty transcriptionOptions/attributeOptions and only `[.volatileResults]` reporting; locale is the sole language control. There is no equivalent of Vision's recognitionLevel (.accurate vs .fast), no usesLanguageCorrection, no customWords/contextualStrings. For concern A this confirms language is entirely locale-driven here; for an OCR fix, the analogous knobs (recognitionLevel = .accurate, recognitionLanguages including zh-Hans/zh-Hant, usesLanguageCorrection) must be set on VNRecognizeTextRequest, which this file does not do but is the pattern to replicate.

Locale identity comparison is brittle: isModelInstalled / isLanguageSupported / currentLanguage matching all compare `Locale.identifier(.bcp47)` against the raw rawValue strings (e.g. "zh-CN"). Apple may return canonicalized identifiers (e.g. "zh-Hans-CN") so `.contains(language.rawValue)` can yield false negatives, blocking download/use of the Chinese model and producing a localeNotSupported error even when Mandarin IS supported. This exact class of locale-string-mismatch bug is a strong candidate for OCR language failures too (zh-Hans vs zh-CN vs zh-Hant-TW).

Audio buffers are dispatched to an unstructured `Task { await self.processAudioBuffer(buffer) }` per tap callback with no ordering guarantee; on the analyzer's AsyncStream this can deliver buffers out of order, degrading recognition quality (a plausible secondary contributor to 'gibberish'-style output for fast/continuous speech). Also `@preconcurrency import AVFoundation` (line 11) suppresses Sendable diagnostics on the buffer crossing actor boundaries.

Download-progress observation uses a manual poll loop (`while !progress.isFinished` with 100ms sleep) inside an untracked detached `Task {}` and also wraps assignments in `MainActor.run` despite the class already being @MainActor. Not language-related but is dead-weight/fragile code; the model-download UX (isModelDownloading/downloadProgress) is the seam an OCR/AI feature would reuse for 'downloading vision model' style progress.

TTS playback hard-codes language codes: `SpeechService.speak(transcript, languageCode: selectedLanguage.rawValue)` and `speakCode = translationDirection == .englishToChinese ? "zh-CN" : "en-US"`. Confirms the app threads BCP-47 language codes through a separate SpeechService (not in this subsystem) — a place where a wrong/locked language choice propagates downstream, same failure shape as A.

Default currentLanguage / startRecording default is `.english` everywhere (property line 79, params lines 256 & 412). The English-first default is structurally why the system 'seems stuck on English' until explicitly overridden — directly the wording of concern A. Any new OCR pipeline should avoid an English-only default and instead pass an array of recognitionLanguages or detect-then-select.

The app has NO NLLanguageRecognizer anywhere; the only language signal is the `isChineseCharacter` scan (LiveSpeechTranslationView.swift:63-65,720) — a robust detector must be added for both speech-language auto-switch and OCR. CONCERN B/C (AI providers): This subsystem contains NO AI-provider abstraction, no API-key storage, and no HTTP request building — it is entirely on-device (SpeechAnalyzer + Apple Translation framework). So there is no provider/model-list code here to extend; that lives elsewhere (e.g. an Ollama service not in these files). Singleton wrapping NaturalLanguage for English: word/POS/lemma tagging (NLTagger forced to .english), sentence splitting, heuristic sentence-type + grammar-point detection, and its own NLLanguageRecognizer-based isEnglish/detectLanguage. keyTypes.name: ChineseTextAnalyzer

keyTypes.name: DetectedLanguage

keyTypes.name: PartOfSpeech

keyTypes.name: EnglishTextAnalyzer

keyTypes.name: EnglishPartOfSpeech

keyTypes.name: PinyinConverter

keyTypes.name: TranslationDirection

keyTypes.name: RubySegment / RubyWordView / WordDetailPopover

keyTypes.name: Character.isChineseCharacter
keyTypes.responsibility: CJK heuristic: scalar in 0x4E00–0x9FFF, 0x3400–0x4DBF, 0x20000–0x2A6DF. The only true character-level CJK signal in the codebase; notably MISSING common ranges (full-width punctuation, CJK Compatibility, Extension B beyond 0x2A6DF endpoint, etc.).

tool_input.dataFlow:
Two parallel detection paths exist, both built on NLLanguageRecognizer. (1) Shortcuts path: ShortcutHelpers.resolveDirection (ShortcutHelpers.swift:34) calls ChineseTextAnalyzer.shared.detectLanguage(text); if .isChinese → chineseToEnglish else default englishToChinese. (2) Photo/OCR path: PhotoTranslateView.processText (PhotoTranslateView.swift:539-569) cleans OCR text, calls its OWN private detectLanguage copy (PhotoTranslateView.swift:573-598), then routes: .english → EnglishTextAnalyzer.analyzeSentences; .chinese → store cleanedChineseText for RubyTextView; .unknown → FALL BACK TO ENGLISH (lines 561-568, and the default branch returns .english). 

Once language is chosen, the analyzers hardcode the NL language: ChineseTextAnalyzer.segmentWithPartsOfSpeech forces tagger.setLanguage(.simplifiedChinese ...) (ChineseTextAnalyzer.swift:38) and segmentWords forces tokenizer.setLanguage(.simplifiedChinese) (line 22); EnglishTextAnalyzer.analyzeWords forces tagger.setLanguage(.english ...) (EnglishTextAnalyzer.swift:224). RubyTextView.updateSegments (RubyTextView.swift:77) feeds the chosen Chinese text into segmentWithPartsOfSpeech, then each RubySegment computes pinyin eagerly via PinyinConverter.convert in its init (RubyTextView.swift:23). PinyinConverter.convert (PinyinConverter.swift:15-20) applies ICU .mandarinToLatin and, for non-Chinese input, returns the input unchanged. Per-word translation is async via WordTranslationService in WordDetailPopover.fetchWordDetails / EnglishWordDetailSheet.translateWord. 

Upstream of all of this, OCR is produced in PhotoTextRecognitionService (recognitionLevel=.accurate, recognitionLanguages=["en-US","en-GB","zh-Hans","zh-Hant"], usesLanguageCorrection=true, VNRecognizeTextRequestRevision3) — English locales are listed FIRST, biasing Vision's language model and language correction toward English even on Mandarin images.

issues.description: recognitionLanguages = ["en-US","en-GB","zh-Hans","zh-Hant"] lists English FIRST. Vision uses array order as a priority/preference hint and combines it with usesLanguageCorrection=true (line 207). For Mandarin images this biases recognition and the language-correction dictionary toward English, producing GIBBERISH (English-looking corrections of Chinese glyphs). There is no language switch / no per-image language selection — the order is static. Root cause of concern A's 'stuck on English / gibberish'. Fix: put zh-Hans/zh-Hant first or make the list user/auto selectable, and consider disabling usesLanguageCorrection for CJK.

Routing fallback hardcodes English: when detectLanguage returns .unknown (or anything non-Chinese), processText runs EnglishTextAnalyzer.analyzeSentences and forces detectedLanguage = .english (lines 561-568). Combined with the private detectLanguage default branch returning .english (line 596), Mandarin OCR that NLLanguageRecognizer fails to classify (common for short/garbled OCR strings) is silently treated as English. This is the 'cannot switch languages' symptom.

Duplicate, divergent language detector: PhotoTranslateView has its OWN private detectLanguage(_:) that is NOT the same as ChineseTextAnalyzer.detectLanguage. It adds a CJK-count heuristic (chineseCharCount > text.count/3, lines 588-596) that ChineseTextAnalyzer lacks, but ONLY in the NLLanguageRecognizer 'default' branch — so if the recognizer confidently mis-detects English, the CJK heuristic never runs. Two detectors with different behavior means OCR routing and shortcut routing disagree. Consolidate into one detector with a CJK-ratio short-circuit applied BEFORE trusting dominantLanguage.

detectLanguage relies solely on NLLanguageRecognizer.dominantLanguage with NO character-level CJK override and NO confidence floor. For short strings, mixed strings, or messy OCR, NLLanguageRecognizer frequently returns .english (or low-confidence garbage) even when Han characters are present. Because Character.isChineseCharacter already exists in this very file (line 184), the fix is to check CJK presence/ratio first and only fall back to the recognizer. This is the central detection bug feeding concern A.

segmentWords (line 22) and segmentWithPartsOfSpeech (line 38) UNCONDITIONALLY setLanguage(.simplifiedChinese). If detection mis-routes English/Traditional text here, or routes garbled OCR here, the tokenizer mis-segments. There is no traditionalChinese handling on the tagger despite detection accepting .traditionalChinese. Mirror issue: EnglishTextAnalyzer.swift:224 unconditionally forces .english.

convert() applies .mandarinToLatin and, for non-Han input, returns the string UNCHANGED (the ?? text and stripDiacritics fallbacks). So when garbled/English OCR is mis-routed into the Chinese ruby path, RubySegment shows the raw garbage as 'pinyin' above itself with no error — the gibberish is rendered, not caught. PinyinConverter has no validation that input is actually Han, so it cannot flag mis-detection.

Second independent detection API (isEnglish at 405, detectLanguage at 412) duplicates ChineseTextAnalyzer's recognizer logic with a different shape (returns NLLanguage). Having three detectors total (here, ChineseTextAnalyzer, PhotoTranslateView) with no shared CJK heuristic is the structural reason language routing is inconsistent and English-biased across the app.

App-wide default direction is .englishToChinese (also @AppStorage defaultDirection across views). Combined with English-first OCR and English fallback routing, the entire pipeline defaults to English at every layer, reinforcing the 'stuck on English' behavior even when the user is scanning Mandarin.

Character.isChineseCharacter covers only 0x4E00-0x9FFF, 0x3400-0x4DBF, 0x20000-0x2A6DF. It MISSES CJK Compatibility Ideographs (0xF900-0xFAFF), full-width/CJK punctuation, and the rest of Extension B+ and later planes. RubySegment.isPunctuation and WordDetailPopover.segmentIsChinese depend on it, so some valid Han characters can be misclassified as punctuation/English at the word level.

pinyinColor in RubyWordView reimplements tone-from-diacritic detection inline (lines 148-163), duplicating PinyinConverter.detectTone/toneColor (PinyinConverter.swift:57-69). Two sources of truth for tone color; a fix to one won't propagate. General maintainability smell that complicates any AI-cleanup integration that would re-render pinyin.

Integration seam for concern C: processText is the single chokepoint where OCR text is cleaned (cleanTextForProcessing) and then detected/routed. An AI-cleanup toggle would slot in here — between cleanTextForProcessing (line 539) and detectLanguage (line 542) — to send the raw OCR string to an AI vision/text model and replace cleanedText with structured/cleaned output before language routing. No abstraction currently exists; the function calls Apple frameworks directly.

WordDetailPopover.fetchWordDetails and EnglishWordDetailSheet.translateWord both call WordTranslationService.shared directly. These per-word translation calls are the natural place to route through a pluggable AI provider (concern B/C), but they are hardwired to one service with no provider abstraction or model selection.

tool_input.integrationPoints:
Concern A (root cause): The detection+routing layer is the heart of the bug. Three things conspire — (1) PhotoTextRecognitionService recognitionLanguages lists English first with usesLanguageCorrection on (PhotoTextRecognitionService.swift:204-207); (2) every analyzer hardcodes its NL language (ChineseTextAnalyzer.swift:22/38, EnglishTextAnalyzer.swift:224); (3) detection trusts NLLanguageRecognizer.dominantLanguage with NO CJK-ratio override and falls back to English on .unknown (ChineseTextAnalyzer.swift:60-76; PhotoTranslateView.swift:561-596). The cleanest fix is a single shared detector that checks Character.isChineseCharacter ratio FIRST (the helper already exists at ChineseTextAnalyzer.swift:184) and only then consults NLLanguageRecognizer, plus reordering/selecting Vision recognitionLanguages per detected/selected language.

Concern B (provider expansion): No provider abstraction lives in this subsystem. The only AI/translation seam visible from here is WordTranslationService.shared, invoked by RubyTextView.WordDetailPopover (RubyTextView.swift:340,346) and EnglishRubyTextView.EnglishWordDetailSheet (EnglishRubyTextView.swift:229). Multi-provider routing (OpenAI/Claude/Deepseek/Doubao/Qwen/Kimi/Zhipu/Minimax) would be introduced behind that service, not in the NL layer. Model-list pulling and API-key storage are out of scope for these files.

Concern C (deep AI integration / photo cleanup toggle): The single best insertion point is PhotoTranslateView.processText (PhotoTranslateView.swift:539-542) — after cleanTextForProcessing and before detectLanguage. A settings toggle would, when ON, route either the raw image or the OCR string to an AI vision/text model and replace cleanedText with cleaned/structured output, then continue into the existing detect→route→render flow (RubyTextView for Chinese, EnglishRubyTextView for English). PinyinConverter and the ruby views consume the cleaned text unchanged, so AI cleanup that yields valid Chinese would automatically flow through to correct pinyin and segmentation.

Shared services: ChineseTextAnalyzer.shared, EnglishTextAnalyzer.shared, PinyinConverter (static), and WordTranslationService.shared are the singletons; DetectedLanguage and TranslationDirection are the routing/data contracts every consumer keys off of.

No photo/OCR cleanup toggle exists in any settings tab. tool_input.dataFlow:
There are THREE distinct OCR/recognition paths, and the language config differs in each.

PATH 1 — Photo picker / single image (PhotoTranslateView):
selectedPhoto change → loadAndProcessImage() loads Data → PhotoTextRecognitionService.recognizeText(from:) → decodes to CGImage → performRecognition(cgImage:) runs ONE VNRecognizeTextRequest (continuation-wrapped) → for each VNRecognizedTextObservation it takes topCandidates(1).first → RecognizedTextBlock → TextRecognitionResult. The view then sets sourceText = result.cleanedText and calls processText(). processText() re-cleans the text, then detectLanguage() via NLLanguageRecognizer decides english vs chinese vs unknown; english → EnglishTextAnalyzer.analyzeSentences; chinese → stores cleanedChineseText for RubyTextView; unknown → falls back to English. Translation is on-demand via Apple Translation framework (translationTask) or WordTranslationService.

KEY VISION CONFIG (PhotoTextRecognitionService.swift, performRecognition, lines 200-212), QUOTED EXACTLY:
  request.recognitionLevel = .accurate                                  (line 201)
  request.recognitionLanguages = ["en-US", "en-GB", "zh-Hans", "zh-Hant"]   (line 204, comment line 203 says "Prioritize English for textbook scanning")
  request.usesLanguageCorrection = true                                 (line 207)
  if #available(iOS 16.0, macOS 13.0, *) { request.revision = VNRecognizeTextRequestRevision3 }   (lines 210-212)
  let handler = VNImageRequestHandler(cgImage: cgImage, options: [:])   (line 214)
Note what is ABSENT: request.automaticallyDetectsLanguage is NEVER set (so on revision 3 it defaults to false because recognitionLanguages is explicitly provided), no orientation passed to the handler, and language order puts en-US/en-GB FIRST.

PATH 2 — Live camera (CameraScannerView, iOS only):
DataScannerViewController(recognizedDataTypes: [.text()], qualityLevel: .accurate, recognizesMultipleItems: true, ...) (lines 39-47). Crucially .text() is called with NO arguments — no textContentType and no languages hint — so it uses system defaults/locale. Coordinator joins RecognizedItem.text transcripts and runs the same English-centric cleanTextForSentences() (duplicated locally, lines 123-143). Output flows via capturedText → PhotoTranslateView.processText().

PATH 3 — Screenshot stitch→translate (ScreenshotTranslationStore.processScreenshots):
pendingImages → ScreenshotStitchingService.stitch() (overlap-detected merge into one tall image) → state .recognizingText → PhotoTextRecognitionService.recognizeText(in: stitched.image) (SAME engine/config as Path 1) → sortInReadingOrder() (groups by Vision boundingBox.maxY rows, sorts X within row) → state .translating → translateBlocks() joins text with "\n§§§\n" delimiter → translateText() builds a TranslationSession with HARDCODED source/target: if target==english source is forced to zh-Hans, else en (lines 295-299) → splits back by delimiter → TranslatedTextBlock[] → TranslatedScreenshotOverlayView renders cards.

Async patterns: OCR uses withCheckedThrowingContinuation around the Vision completion handler; all three services are @MainActor @Observable singletons; image work is awaited but Vision perform([request]) runs synchronously on the calling (main) actor inside the continuation. Translation uses async TranslationSession.
tool_input.integrationPoints:
CONCERN A (gibberish + cannot switch language) — root causes, ranked:
1. PhotoTextRecognitionService.swift:204 hardcodes recognitionLanguages = ["en-US","en-GB","zh-Hans","zh-Hant"] with English FIRST and never sets request.automaticallyDetectsLanguage. With VNRecognizeTextRequestRevision3 (line 211), supplying an explicit recognitionLanguages array disables automatic detection; ordering biases the recognizer toward English, so Chinese pages get mis-segmented into Latin-looking garbage ("gibberish") and the result reads as English. There is NO API to change languages at call time — it is a fixed literal, so the feature genuinely "cannot switch languages." FIX SEAM: make recognitionLanguages a parameter, set request.automaticallyDetectsLanguage = true (and pass [] / detected language), or run a detection pass and re-OCR with zh-Hans first.
2. usesLanguageCorrection = true (line 207) applies English-model autocorrection that mangles Chinese/pinyin and OCR of mixed text — should be conditional on detected language.
3. TextRecognitionResult.cleanedText (lines 45-72) and the duplicated cleaners in PhotoTranslateView (601-621) and CameraScannerView (123-143) are English-centric: they collapse ALL whitespace to single spaces, strip "- ", and add spaces around A-Z after .?! — these transforms are wrong for Chinese and further corrupt mixed text.
4. Language detection runs AFTER OCR (PhotoTranslateView.detectLanguage via NLLanguageRecognizer, lines 573-598). Because OCR already produced English-biased gibberish, NLLanguageRecognizer then "confirms" English (the >count/3 CJK heuristic at 593 rarely triggers on gibberish), explaining the "stuck on English" symptom. TextRecognitionResult.language is hardwired to nil (line 40), so detection is never carried with the OCR result.
5. CameraScannerView uses .text() with no language hint (line 40) — same locale-default lock, independent of the above.

CONCERN B (expand providers + pull model lists) — seams:
- AIProvider enum (AIModelSettings.swift:15-47) currently has ONLY .appleIntelligence and .ollama; this is the enum to extend with .openAI/.anthropic/.deepseek/.doubao/.qwen/.kimi/.zhipu/.minimax.
- AIModelSettings persists only provider/ollamaModel/ollamaHost/thinking/contextLength via UserDefaults (Keys enum 60-66). There is NO apiKey storage anywhere (no Keychain usage found) — must be added (Keychain recommended, not UserDefaults).
- OllamaService.refreshModels() (110-152) is the existing "pull available models from the provider API" pattern (client.listModels() + per-model capability probe) to replicate per provider (e.g. GET /v1/models for OpenAI-compatible endpoints; most of the listed Chinese providers expose OpenAI-compatible /models endpoints).
- OllamaService.chat()/generateStructured()/translate() (164-328) show the request-building + system/user message shape to generalize behind a provider protocol. effectiveProvider/statusMessage/refreshConnection (123-196) are the connection-status patterns to mirror.

CONCERN C (AI cleanup of uploaded photo via toggle) — seams:
- The cleanest insertion point is between OCR and downstream processing. In PhotoTranslateView.loadAndProcessImage() (496-524): after `let result = try await PhotoTextRecognitionService.shared.recognizeText(from: data)` (508) and before `sourceText = result.cleanedText` (512), if an 'AI cleanup' toggle is ON, route result.fullText (or the raw image) to the selected AI provider and use the cleaned/structured text instead.
- The toggle itself belongs in the existing toolbar Menu in PhotoTranslateView.body (lines 102-120, alongside showGrammarPoints), and its persisted backing belongs in AIModelSettings.
- A vision-capable provider could replace OCR entirely: ScreenshotStitchingService produces stitched.image (UIImage/NSImage) and ScreenshotTranslationStore.processScreenshots() (156-189) calls recognizeText(in: stitched.image) at line 172 — that call site can branch to an AI vision model that takes the image directly and returns structured text, skipping Vision OCR.
- No provider abstraction supports image input today (OllamaService is text-only), so concern C depends on concern B's multi-provider/vision plumbing.
- Persistence layer is UserDefaults-only via AIModelSettings; ScreenshotTranslationStore/PhotoTextRecognitionService are the shared services AI cleanup would hook into.

issues.description: recognitionLanguages is a hardcoded literal ["en-US","en-GB","zh-Hans","zh-Hant"] with English first and no way to override per-call. Combined with the missing automaticallyDetectsLanguage flag (never set), VNRecognizeTextRequestRevision3 treats the explicit array as authoritative and biases recognition toward English, producing gibberish on Chinese pages and making language 'unswitchable'. This is the primary root cause of concern A.

request.automaticallyDetectsLanguage is never set anywhere in the request configuration. On revision 3 it defaults to false when recognitionLanguages is supplied, so Vision cannot auto-detect Chinese vs English. There is also no detect-then-reOCR pass. Fix requires either enabling automatic detection or running language detection on a cheap pass and re-running OCR with the correct language ordering.

usesLanguageCorrection = true is applied unconditionally. English autocorrection corrupts Chinese and mixed CN/EN OCR output, contributing to gibberish. Should be disabled or made conditional on detected language.

cleanTextForSentences is English-centric: collapses all whitespace to single spaces, strips '- ', and inserts spaces around capital letters after .?!. For Chinese (which has no spaces and uses full-width punctuation 。？！) these transforms damage the text. The same cleaner is duplicated in PhotoTranslateView.cleanTextForProcessing (601-621) and CameraScannerView.cleanTextForSentences (123-143) — three copies to keep consistent.

Language detection (NLLanguageRecognizer) runs AFTER OCR on already-English-biased output, so it confirms English and the CJK-fraction fallback (line 593, chineseCharCount > text.count/3) rarely fires on gibberish. Detection should happen before/at OCR (ideally on the image) and drive recognitionLanguages, not after.

TextRecognitionResult.language is hardcoded to nil and never populated, so detected language is never carried with the OCR result downstream. Per-observation language is also discarded (only topCandidates(1).string/confidence kept, lines 186-195).

DataScannerViewController is created with recognizedDataTypes: [.text()] — .text() called with no arguments means no language hint, so live camera OCR is locked to system/locale defaults and is a second independent path that 'cannot switch languages'. Use .text(languages:) to pass Chinese.

VNImageRequestHandler is created with options:[:] and no orientation. UIImage.imageOrientation / EXIF orientation is ignored, so rotated photos OCR poorly — another gibberish contributor for camera-captured photos.

AIProvider enum only models .appleIntelligence and .ollama. There is no abstraction for remote providers (OpenAI/Claude/Deepseek/Doubao/Qwen/Kimi/Zhipu/Minimax) and no per-provider config, base URL, or model field. This enum + AIModelSettings must be expanded and a provider protocol introduced for concern B.

No API-key storage exists anywhere (UserDefaults Keys cover only provider/model/host/thinking/contextLength; no Keychain usage found in the codebase). Adding cloud providers requires secure key storage — recommend Keychain, not UserDefaults.

refreshModels() is the only 'pull model list from provider API' implementation (client.listModels() + per-model showModel capability probe). For concern B this pattern must be generalized: most listed providers expose an OpenAI-compatible GET /v1/models endpoint, but each needs its own client/auth. Currently model discovery is Ollama-specific.

Request building (chat/generateStructured/translate) is tightly coupled to the Ollama Swift SDK types (Ollama.Model.ID, Ollama.Chat.Message, Ollama.Value) and is text-only with no image/vision input. A provider-neutral protocol with image support is required for concerns B and C.

loadAndProcessImage has no AI-cleanup hook. The ideal insertion point for concern C is right after recognizeText(from:) at line 508 and before sourceText = result.cleanedText at 512: when an 'AI cleanup' toggle is ON, send result.fullText (or the image) to the selected AI provider and substitute the cleaned/structured result. No such toggle or branch exists today.

processScreenshots calls PhotoTextRecognitionService.recognizeText(in: stitched.image) directly with no option to route to an AI vision model. This single call site is the seam where a vision-capable provider (concern C) could replace Vision OCR entirely, taking stitched.image and returning structured text.

translateText hardcodes the language pair: if target==english, source is forced to zh-Hans, else en. This bidirectional assumption breaks for non-CN/EN content and is brittle if OCR returns the wrong language; an AI provider path (B/C) could remove this assumption.

getPixelData forces sRGB + premultipliedLast and the overlap detector (findOverlapHeight, 273-341) samples RGB with a 0.90 similarity threshold; an incorrect overlap removal can crop real content out of the stitched image fed to OCR, indirectly degrading recognition quality (general; can compound concern A on stitched screenshots).

Because it is CaseIterable and drives the settings Picker and effectiveProvider switch, adding cases ripples through the whole app automatically.

keyTypes.name: AIModelSettings

Notably stores ONLY Ollama-shaped config (ollamaModel, ollamaHost, enableThinking, contextLength) — there is NO apiKey storage and NO per-provider model/baseURL maps. effectiveProvider only knows how to fall back between Apple and Ollama.

keyTypes.name: OllamaService
keyTypes.responsibility: @Observable @MainActor singleton. Concrete provider client. Holds a private `Ollama.Client`; exposes availableModels:[OllamaModelInfo], isConnected, connectionError. keyTypes.name: Ollama.Client (third-party, ollama-swift)

Cannot reach OpenAI/Anthropic/cloud APIs that require API keys and different endpoints. New cloud providers cannot reuse this client; they need their own URLSession request builders.

keyTypes.name: OllamaModelInfo

keyTypes.name: WordExplanation / ExampleSentence / RelatedWord / Collocation

Mirrored by a hand-written JSON schema (Ollama path) and by OllamaWordExplanationResponse for decoding. Any new provider must emit JSON conforming to the same shape that maps to WordExplanationResult.

keyTypes.name: WordExplanationResult + *Result structs
keyTypes.responsibility: Provider-neutral output DTO consumed by the UI. Both Apple and Ollama paths converge here. This is the stable contract; new providers should also produce WordExplanationResult.

keyTypes.name: AIWordExplanationService

This switch is the single chokepoint where every new provider case must be handled — and where a photo-cleanup entry point (concern C) belongs.

keyTypes.name: OllamaWordExplanationResponse
keyTypes.responsibility: Codable decoder for Ollama's JSON structured output, with toResult(filteringFor:) that filters example sentences/collocations to those literally containing the target word. Reusable for any provider returning the same JSON shape.

keyTypes.name: AIExplanationError / OllamaServiceError
keyTypes.responsibility: LocalizedError enums. Both are Ollama/Apple-specific (e.g. ollamaNotConnected, ollamaNoModelSelected). New providers would need analogous error cases or a generalized provider-error type.

keyTypes.name: WordTranslationService
keyTypes.responsibility: @Observable singleton using Apple Translation framework (TranslationSession) for per-word zh<->en translation with a string cache. Independent of the AI-provider stack; not a plug-in seam for B.

tool_input.dataFlow:
PROVIDER SELECTION & DISPATCH: UI (MacOSSettingsView Picker, line ~115) binds to AIModelSettings.shared.provider; didSet persists to UserDefaults. At call time AIWordExplanationView.generateExplanation() -> aiService.generateExplanationWithProvider() -> reads AIModelSettings.shared.effectiveProvider -> switch routes to (a) generateExplanation (Apple: LanguageModelSession(instructions:).respond(to:generating:WordExplanation.self)) or (b) generateExplanationWithOllama (builds a hand-written Ollama.Value JSON schema, calls OllamaService.generateStructured -> client.chat(model:messages:options:format:think:keepAlive:) -> decodes OllamaWordExplanationResponse -> toResult(filteringFor: word)). Both converge on WordExplanationResult, cached in explanationCache keyed by word_pinyin_context. 

OLLAMA REQUEST BUILDING: OllamaService.chat() constructs Model.ID(rawValue: model)! (force-unwrap), messages = [.system(systemPrompt), .user(userPrompt)], calls client.chat with options (defaultOptions: num_ctx 128000, temperature 0.7, top_p 0.9, repeat_penalty 1.1, num_predict -1), think: enableThinking, keepAlive: .minutes(10). Structured path adds format: schema and uses reasoningOptions (temp 0.3). The underlying Ollama.Client.createRequest() POSTs JSON to Ollama-native /api/* paths with ONLY Accept/User-Agent/Content-Type headers — no auth. 

MODEL LISTING: AIModelSettings.refreshConnection() -> OllamaService.checkConnection() (client.version()) then refreshModels() -> client.listModels(), and for each model client.showModel(Model.ID(...)!) to read capabilities (.thinking/.tools); builds [OllamaModelInfo] sorted by name; surfaced to the Settings model Picker via ollamaService.availableModels. So model lists ARE already pulled live from the provider API — but only via the Ollama endpoint shape. 

KEY/HOST STORAGE: ollamaHost stored in UserDefaults (default http://localhost:11434); its didSet calls updateOllamaServiceHost() which rebuilds OllamaService.shared.hostURL -> new Ollama.Client(host:). There is NO API key storage anywhere (no Keychain, no UserDefaults key). 

ASYNC PATTERNS: Everything is async/await on @MainActor singletons; OCR (PhotoTextRecognitionService) bridges Vision's callback API via withCheckedThrowingContinuation.

issues.description: recognitionLanguages is hardcoded to ["en-US","en-GB","zh-Hans","zh-Hant"] with English FIRST and usesLanguageCorrection=true (line 207). Vision uses language-list ORDER as a strong prior; with English first and language correction on, Chinese text is frequently mis-recognized as English-like gibberish and the user cannot 'switch' to Chinese because the order is fixed in code with no UI/parameter. This is the root cause of concern A (gibberish + stuck on English). Fix: make recognitionLanguages dynamic/user-selectable (or detect script and reorder, putting zh-Hans/zh-Hant first for Chinese), and consider disabling usesLanguageCorrection for CJK.

There is NO API key storage of any kind (no Keychain, no UserDefaults key). The Keys enum only has provider/ollamaModel/ollamaHost/enableThinking/contextLength. Cloud providers (OpenAI, Claude, Deepseek, etc.) all require API keys, so concern B is blocked until secure per-provider key storage (ideally Keychain) is added.

AIProvider is a closed 2-case enum (only apple + ollama). Every provider-aware switch in the codebase (effectiveProvider, statusMessage, generateExplanationWithProvider, translateWithProvider, settings UI) is exhaustive on these two cases, so concern B requires expanding this enum AND updating every switch. The settings UI also assumes Ollama-only fields (host/model/context) inside `if settings.provider == .ollama`.

The entire AI provider layer is hard-bound to the third-party Ollama.Client, whose init accepts only host+userAgent and whose createRequest() sets no Authorization header (verified at ollama-swift Client.swift:36-47/231-241) and hardcodes Ollama-native /api/* paths. This client cannot call OpenAI/Anthropic/cloud endpoints. There is no provider-protocol abstraction; OllamaService is concrete. Concern B needs a new AIProviderClient protocol + custom URLSession request builders per provider (most are OpenAI-compatible; Anthropic differs).

generateExplanationWithProvider/translateWithProvider are the single dispatch chokepoint but switch only over apple/ollama. There is no method that accepts/cleans up OCR text or photo images, so concern C has no entry point yet. This service is where a cleanupRecognizedText / vision-cleanup method should be added and routed through the (expanded) provider switch.

effectiveProvider only knows fallback between Apple Intelligence and Ollama and treats 'available' as Ollama.isConnected. For cloud providers, 'available' should mean a valid API key + reachable endpoint. This logic must be generalized when concern B providers are added, or cloud providers will be wrongly considered unavailable/never selected.

ollamaOptions and OllamaService.defaultOptions/reasoningOptions are Ollama-specific (num_ctx, top_p, repeat_penalty, num_predict, think). These do not map cleanly to OpenAI/Anthropic request params (max_tokens, temperature, top_p, response_format/tools). A provider-neutral generation-options abstraction is needed for concern B so each client can translate options to its own API.

client.showModel(Ollama.Model.ID(rawValue: model.name)!) and chat/generateStructured all force-unwrap Model.ID(rawValue:)! (also lines 171,197,230). A model name that the SPM library considers invalid will crash. When concern B adds arbitrary cloud model IDs (e.g. 'gpt-4o', 'claude-3-5-sonnet'), reusing this ID type / force-unwrap pattern is unsafe.

Ollama structured output is decoded strictly with JSONDecoder().decode(OllamaWordExplanationResponse.self). Cloud models often wrap JSON in markdown fences or prose; without extraction/repair this decode will throw for many providers. Concern B/C needs tolerant JSON extraction (strip ```json fences, find first {...}).

Uses TranslationSession(installedSource: zh-Hans, target: en) with hardcoded language pairs requiring pre-downloaded packs; throws if packs are not installed. Separate from the AI stack but relevant to the broader translation/language-switch UX referenced in concern A. Not a provider seam.

isAnyProviderAvailable checks only isAppleIntelligenceAvailable || OllamaService.shared.isConnected. After concern B, this gate must also recognize configured cloud providers, or the AI UI will show 'AI Not Available' even when a cloud key is set.
Default ollamaModel is hardcoded to 'gpt-oss:20b' and resetToDefaults re-applies it. With multiple providers, a single global default model is ambiguous; defaults should be per-provider.

issues.description: Language pair is HARD-CODED to English<->Simplified-Chinese only. detectedTranslationDirection derives direction solely from containsChinese(sourceText), and TranslationSession.Configuration is built from TranslationDirection.sourceLanguage/targetLanguage fixed to Locale.Language('en') and 'zh-Hans'. No mechanism to switch to or detect any other language, and no NLLanguageRecognizer is used. This is a structural root of concern A 'cannot switch languages / stuck on English': any OCR/pasted text not containing a CJK char is forced onto the en->zh-Hans path, so mis-OCR'd Mandarin (garbled to latin-ish glyphs) or any non-EN/non-ZH text is treated as English source.

AI provider abstraction is binary and closed: translateWithProvider only routes to Apple Intelligence (Foundation Models) or Ollama (translateWithOllama -> OllamaService.shared). No provider enum/registry, no OpenAI/Anthropic/Deepseek/Doubao/Qwen/Kimi/Zhipu/Minimax path, and no way to pull a remote model list. To satisfy concern B, a provider protocol + per-provider request builder + model-list fetch must be introduced and translateWithProvider (and the explanation path) re-pointed at it.

The AI translation seam passes only (text, sourceIsChinese: Bool) and returns a plain String. There is no image/vision parameter, no API-key plumbing, and no structured/cleaned-text return path. For concern C (route an uploaded photo to an AI vision/text model for cleanup), this seam needs a vision-capable variant (e.g. cleanupImage(_:)->String or cleanup(rawOCRText:)) and a settings toggle gating it. The @AppStorage toggles read here (autoTranslate, translateOnPaste, copyTranslationAutomatically, saveToHistoryAutomatically, defaultDirection at lines 31-35) are the natural place to add an 'AI cleanup' toggle.

Chinese detection everywhere relies on $0.isChineseCharacter / containsChinese. Fragile: cannot distinguish Simplified vs Traditional, treats any CJK char as 'Chinese', and yields no confidence score. NLLanguageRecognizer (with languageHints/dominantLanguage) is the correct API and is conspicuously absent across this subsystem — relevant because the OCR gibberish problem (A) is masked and compounded by this heuristic language classification driving translation direction.

History persistence stores the ENTIRE entry array as one JSON blob in UserDefaults on every add/remove/move (O(n) serialize-on-write; UserDefaults is not meant for large payloads). If AI features (B/C) increase translation volume this degrades. No schema versioning on the Codable model.

load() uses try? JSONDecoder().decode(...); any schema change to TranslationHistoryEntry (likely when adding multi-language/provider metadata for B/C) silently discards the ENTIRE history rather than migrating. No model versioning.

TranslationState is a non-isolated @Observable singleton mutated from MainActor.run blocks and SwiftUI bindings but is NOT @MainActor (unlike TranslationHistoryStore which is). Future async network providers (B) writing back results off the main actor could create data races on sourceText/translatedText.

preserveCurrentTranslationDuringSourceUpdate uses DispatchQueue.main.async to clear a flag — a timing hack that can race with rapid programmatic source updates. Injecting cleaned text from an AI photo pipeline (C) into sharedState.sourceText may inadvertently trip the onChange clear logic at lines 276-296.

Single shared AVSpeechSynthesizer; speak() always stopSpeaking(.immediate) first so concurrent source+target speech is impossible, and language is taken from direction.*SpeechCode (zh-CN/en-US only) — same EN/ZH-only limitation. No error surfaced when a voice for the language code is unavailable.

Apple Translation errors are string-matched (lines 935-936: errorDescription.contains('language')/'unavailable') to produce a 'download language pack' message. Brittle/locale-dependent; if OCR feeds an unsupported language the user gets a confusing 'language pack' error rather than 'unsupported language', masking concern A's real cause.

tool_input.dataFlow: Two distinct pipelines. On any AI error it silently falls through to translateWithRetry() which builds a fresh `TranslationSession(installedSource:target:)` per attempt (up to 3 tries, 200ms backoff) against Apple's Translation framework. Result + usedAI flag bubble back; intents then write TranslationHistoryStore.shared.add and optionally ShortcutHelpers.saveChinesePhrasesToVocabulary (which segments via ChineseTextAnalyzer.segmentWithPartsOfSpeech, then batch/one-by-one translates via WordTranslationService.shared and persists SavedTerm via PinyinConverter + SavedTermsStore). Async patterns: all text intents are @MainActor with async perform; vocabulary saving spawns detached Task; EntityQuery bodies hop to MainActor.run to read singleton stores. issues.description: Hardcoded recognitionLanguages = ["en-US", "en-GB", "zh-Hans", "zh-Hant"] with English listed FIRST and usesLanguageCorrection=true. Vision uses language order as a strong prior; English-first plus language correction makes the recognizer bias toward English and 'correct' Chinese glyphs into Latin gibberish. There is no automaticallyDetectsLanguage and no way for the Translate Screenshots intent (whose ShortcutTargetLanguage is only english/chinese) to reorder/restrict languages. This is the prime root cause of concern A (gibberish + cannot switch to Chinese). The intent's targetLanguage parameter is passed to ScreenshotTranslationStore for translation only and never influences OCR recognitionLanguages.

translateWithProvider switches over AIModelSettings.effectiveProvider with only two cases: .appleIntelligence and .ollama. Every shortcut AI path (ShortcutHelpers.aiTranslate) funnels through here, so providers like OpenAI/Claude/Deepseek/Doubao/Qwen/Kimi/Zhipu/Minimax cannot be reached from Shortcuts. Adding them requires extending the provider enum + effectiveProvider + this switch (and ShortcutHelpers.aiIsAvailable at ShortcutHelpers.swift:95 which also only checks Apple Intelligence || Ollama).

aiIsAvailable() is hardcoded to `AIModelSettings.shared.isAppleIntelligenceAvailable || OllamaService.shared.isConnected`. Even after adding cloud providers, the shortcut AI toggle would report 'unavailable' for them and silently fall back to Apple Translation, so concern B work must update this gate too. The user-facing parameter is even labeled 'Use Apple Intelligence' (TranslateTextIntent.swift:18, etc.), which is misleading once multiple providers exist.

AI translation failures are swallowed by an empty catch (`} catch { // Fall through ... }`) that discards the error and falls back to the Translation framework. For concern B/C this hides provider/API-key/network errors (e.g. a misconfigured OpenAI key) making provider debugging impossible from Shortcuts; at minimum the error should be logged.

processScreenshots() is launched in a detached `Task { await store.processScreenshots() }` while perform() returns immediately with a dialog. The OCR/translate result is not surfaced through the intent's return value (intent returns `some IntentResult` with no value), so a Shortcut cannot chain the recognized/translated/AI-cleaned text. For concern C (route photo to AI and 'return cleaned/structured text to the app'), this intent has no return-value channel to hand cleaned text back to a Shortcut; it only deep-links into the UI.

ShortcutTargetLanguage only supports english and chinese (binary). Combined with the English-first OCR config, there is no Shortcut-level affordance to force Chinese-source recognition or any other language, reinforcing the 'cannot switch languages' symptom. A source-language / recognition-language parameter is missing.

resolveDirection() for .auto relies solely on ChineseTextAnalyzer.shared.detectLanguage(text).isChinese (NLLanguageRecognizer-based, ChineseTextAnalyzer.swift:61/79). If OCR already produced English gibberish from Chinese input, detection sees Latin text and routes englishToChinese, compounding concern A end-to-end (wrong OCR -> wrong language detection -> wrong translation direction).

parameterSummary uses double-escaped interpolation `Summary("Translate \\(\\.$images) to \\(\\.$targetLanguage)")`, which will render literal backslashes/parens in the Shortcuts summary instead of the parameter tokens. Cosmetic but user-visible bug in the screenshot intent UI.

saveChinesePhrasesToVocabulary spawns a fire-and-forget `Task { await translateAndSaveWords(...) }` whose result/errors are never observed by the calling intent; vocabulary saves can silently fail or race after the intent reports success. name: build-and-project-structure
description: How to build SwiftMandarin, its sandbox/network entitlement, and how new Swift files get into the build
metadata:

---

SwiftMandarin is a single-target multiplatform SwiftUI app (iOS/macOS/visionOS **26.2** deploy targets, Swift 5 mode, Xcode 26.3). One SPM dependency: `ollama-swift 1.8.0`.

**Build/verify commands (both pass clean):**
- macOS: `xcodebuild -scheme SwiftMandarin -destination 'platform=macOS' -configuration Debug build CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`
- iOS: `xcodebuild -scheme SwiftMandarin -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' -configuration Debug build CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`

**New Swift files:** the target uses `fileSystemSynchronizedGroups = (SwiftMandarin)`, so any `.swift` file added under `SwiftMandarin/` is auto-included in the build — no `project.pbxproj` editing needed. (There are also ~24 legacy explicit file refs in the pbxproj; leave them, Xcode 26 dedupes by path.)

**Sandbox:** `ENABLE_APP_SANDBOX = YES`. The entitlements file is `SwiftMandarin/SwiftMandarin.entitlements`. Outbound networking (Ollama on macOS, all cloud AI providers) REQUIRES `com.apple.security.network.client` — this was missing and added 2026-06-04. Info.plist is generated (`GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE=YES`) via `INFOPLIST_KEY_*` build settings; note `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription`/`NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription` are currently empty strings (latent iOS crash risk if speech permission is requested).

State pattern: `@Observable @MainActor` singletons (`.shared`) over UserDefaults JSON; stores injected via `.environment(...)` in `SwiftMandarinApp`, but `AIModelSettings.shared`/`AppPreferences.shared` are reached as singletons inside views. See [[ai-provider-architecture]].
